cfg.runtime: Where the dsh agent process runs. 'auto' = same side as the extension host. Use 'wsl' from Windows VS Code to run dsh inside WSL; use 'windows' from a Remote-WSL window to run dsh on Windows.
cfg.runtime.auto: Same side as the extension host
cfg.runtime.wsl: Inside WSL (valid when the extension host runs on Windows)
cfg.runtime.windows: On Windows (valid when the extension host runs inside WSL)
cfg.command: Command used to launch dsh on the target side; the extension appends `--profile <dsh.profile>`. Examples: `npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh`, `dsh`, `node ~/deepseek-harness/apps/cli/lib/bin.js`.
cfg.wslDistro: WSL distribution name used when dsh.runtime is 'wsl'. Empty = default distribution.
cfg.env: Extra environment variables for the dsh process (e.g. `{ "DEEPSEEK_API_KEY": "..." }`).
cfg.autoAttach: Automatically attach the active editor file (and selection) as context to each prompt.
cfg.mcpServers: MCP servers mounted on every new dsh session. stdio: `{name, command, args?, env?}`; http: `{name, type: "http", url, headers?}`. Prefer `DSH: Configure MCP Servers`.
cfg.profile: dsh profile to boot. Default `acp-vscode`, created by the required dsh-vscode-bridge plugin install (`DSH: Install/Repair Bridge Plugin`). `acp` runs bridge-less (no titles/delete/presets/permissions/workspace grouping).
